thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p99 latency breach detected for route /v1/generate in prod us-east-1. p99=3.6s (SLO=2.0s). Alert triggered 2026-03-15T10:12:30Z. paging: oncall-sre.

alex: I'm alive, getting the alert. going to pull dashboards. anyone already on it?

priya: I'm here, 10:12. seeing a sustained tail spike on streaming requests. p95 up to 1.2s but p99 spiking to 3.6s.

sam: confirmed. Datadog shows a sudden increase in long-tail durations starting ~10:09.

jorge: tagging eng-runtime & eng-sre. @oncall-sre please coordinate.

oncall-sre: oncall-sre here. assigning initial roles: alex lead triage, priya customer-impact, sam runtime checks, jorge logs + routing, lina to coordinate mitigations.

lina: noted. starting mitigation doc in thread.

alex: quick checks: 1) origin infra CPU/GPU 2) kvcache hitrate 3) request queue depth 4) recent deploys. I'm running the queries now.

sam: GPU util in us-east-1 nodes normal ~65%. no obvious saturation.

jorge: log grep shows repeated streamer stalls on host inference-42: "stall_detected: stream idle > 2s, flush triggered". small fraction of hosts showing many stalls.

priya: customer-impact: internal telemetry (route=/v1/generate, tier=hosted) shows 4% requests >2s last 5m. Some streaming sessions dropped mid-response, customers saw partial output. I'm compiling impacted customer IDs.

emma: I'm monitoring public-facing health page; no major errors but latency banner might be needed.

alex: Datadog queries I'm running:```text
avg:last_1m:service.request.latency{route:/v1/generate,env:prod}.percentile(99)
count:last_5m:service.stream.stalls{env:prod}
```
Initial p99 series: 1.8s -> 2.6s -> 3.6s. stalls count increased ~6x.

sam: checking model variants: traffic shows 85% on rwd-xl-2026 and 15% fallback rwd-xl-quant. No recent deploys to these variants in last hour.

jorge: KV cache miss rate jumped from 12% to 48% on the affected pool. looks like cache churn.

lina: Is the cache eviction policy behaving weird? recent rollout to kvcache-evict-v2 yesterday?

alex: good catch. there was a config change for kvcache eviction last night in dedicated. ops config shows a rollout to prod-evict v2 at 02:00 UTC. tagging it as potential root.

oncall-sre: next steps: 1) roll back kvcache eviction change on affected pool (if safe) 2) scale out inference nodes in us-east-1 3) enable streaming fallbacks (chunked flush) temporarily 4) notify customers. who's on rollback?

sam: I'll prep the rollback. doing a dry-run and will push to canary host first (inference-42).

priya: I'll draft customer note: short blurb + mitigation ETA. want to be conservative on impact numbers.

alex: while sam does rollback, lina please increase pool capacity by +2 nodes and switch routing to spread across healthy AZs. command:```bash
redwood infra scale --pool inference-prod-us-east-1 --add-nodes 2
```

lina: running scale now. expected node join in ~90s.

jorge: routing change: moving 20% traffic off pool us-east-1-a to us-east-1-b to reduce load on hosts with stalls. executing route update.

sam: canary rollback applied to inference-42: reverting kvcache-evict to previous policy. monitoring logs...

sam: logs: stall events on inference-42 dropped from 7/min to 1/min after rollback. p99 on that host dropped from 4.2s to 1.5s.

priya: customer-impact note: "We're investigating increased response times for streaming requests in us-east-1. Some customers experienced partial responses. We're rolling mitigations now and will update in 30m." posting to status page?

emma: go ahead, post short status. add link to internal triage thread. I posted maintenance banner.

alex: global p99 trending down: 3.6 -> 2.5 -> 1.9 over last 6 minutes. good sign. keep actions for 10 more minutes and then evaluate.

oncall-sre: continue monitoring. Lina confirm scale completed?

lina: new nodes joined and passed readiness checks. load rebalanced.

jorge: full pool kvcache missrate trending back to 15% after rollback + scale.

priya: customer list: 4 customers reported via support with partial streaming; support already issued workaround to re-request. marking P2 for follow-up.

alex: check streaming pipeline for any backpressure from fronting proxies.

sam: proxy queue depth normal. no backlog. the main vector was kvcache eviction combined with a small subset of nodes having increased stall vulnerabilities.

oncall-sre: mitigation summary: reverted kvcache eviction config on affected pool, scaled +2 nodes, redistributed traffic across AZs, enabled temporary streaming chunk flush fallback. Immediate impact resolved (p99 back under SLO).

priya: publishing customer update with root-cause summary once postmortem ready.

alex: recommending follow-ups: 1) revert rollout plan for kvcache evict v2 and run canary with higher coverage tests 2) add alert for sudden global kvcache miss-rate spikes 3) add guardrail to avoid single-AZ routing concentration during rollouts 4) investigate why eviction policy caused disproportionate stall cascade.

lina: I'll create the follow-up tasks and assign to runtime/infra.

oncall-sre: incident state -> mitigated. continuing watch for 30 min. handing off to daytime oncall for long-term monitoring.

alex: handing to daytime oncall @sam in 15m. please pick up any residual.

sam: acknowledged handoff. will monitor dashboards and escalate if p99 > 2.0s again.

priya: final customer-impact note queued for 30m with link to postmortem draft.

emma: thanks all. quick retro: we should have a preflight test for kvcache eviction changes.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager duty page resolved for alert id PD-38921.

oncall-sre: closing thread, creating incident ticket: INC-2026-0315-01 and postmortem placeholder.

alex: nice work team. :thumbsup:
